# Ping Xintao

Chinese literary scholar, writer, and editor-in-chief

![Image 1](https://gbaike-image.cdn.bcebos.com/f636afc379310a557591c1ebbd4543a982261073/f636afc379310a557591c1ebbd4543a982261073_url?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto/resize,m_lfit,w_400,limit_1)

Ping Xintao (June 26, 1927 – May 23, 2019), male, was born in Changshu City, Jiangsu Province, graduated from Shanghai Datong University, and was a Chinese writer, author, and editor-in-chief. He was the husband of Taiwanese author Qiong Yao, the founder of the Crown Cultural Group, and founded the Crown Magazine Agency and the Crown Publishing House.

5

Ping Xintao loved literature and art from a young age. Due to his father's demand, he studied in the Department of Accounting at Shanghai Datong University. After graduation, he moved to Taipei in 1949 and worked at the Taiwan Fertilizer Company. On February 22, 1954, he founded the Crown magazine and established the Crown Publishing House in the same year. To subsidize the cost of publishing the magazine, in addition to translating novels under the pen name "Fei Li", he also hosted a Western pop music program on a radio station. In June 1963, Ping Xintao became the concurrent editor-in-chief of the "United Daily News Literary Supplement" in the United Daily News. In October of the following year, he established a "featured writer" system for the Crown magazine, providing advance payment for manuscripts, thereby recruiting and nurturing talented writers of the time, and gradually building "Crown" into a publishing empire renowned throughout the Chinese-speaking world. Subsequently, Ping Xintao expanded into film, television, music records, and established multiple companies. In the 1990s, he entered the film and television industry together with his wife Qiong Yao, specializing in adapting her novels into films and TV dramas. Starting from 1998, Ping Xintao served as the producer for the TV dramas My Fair Princess, Princess of Pearl 2, and My Fair Princess III: Heaven and Earth. In 2002, Ping Xintao received the Literary and Art Award Medal from the Chinese Literary and Art Association. He died of illness on May 23, 2019, at the age of 92.

1

Throughout his life, Ping Xintao edited newspapers for over 5,000 days, published 784 issues of magazines and more than 6,000 book series, and produced 16 films and over 600 hours of TV series. The Crown magazine and Crown Publishing House under his leadership won the Golden Tripod Award four times. In 2005, the Crown Cultural Group received special commendation from the Taipei City Government for its outstanding publishing achievements and profound literary contributions.

Biography

Early Years

Ping Xintao loved literature and art from a young age. He originally intended to study painting at the Hangzhou Academy of Fine Arts, but due to his father's demands, he switched to majoring in accounting at Shanghai Datong University. After graduating from university, Ping Xintao went to Taiwan in 1949 to work at the Taiwan Fertilizer Company.

6

Middle Years

On February 22, 1954, Ping Xintao founded Crown Magazine and established the Crown Publishing House in the same year. To subsidize the expenses of publishing the magazine, in addition to translating novels under the pen name "Fei Li," he also hosted a popular Western music program on a radio station, coining the term "Hot Music." In June 1963, Ping Xintao succeeded as the editor-in-chief of the United Daily News Literary Supplement in Taiwan, a position he held until January 1976. In October 1964, he established the "Crown Basic Writer System," providing advance payments to cultivate talented and promising writers. Beyond serving as the primary platform for Qiong Yao's rise to prominence and long-term success, the system also introduced the works of Eileen Chang to Taiwan and gathered renowned writers such as Sima Zhongyuan, Zhu Xining, San Mao, Ji Ji, Ni Kuang, Lin Huaimin, Zhang Manjuan, and Hou Wenyong. This was an unprecedented initiative in Taiwan's publishing and literary circles at the time, celebrated as a remarkable achievement, and gradually built "Crown" into a publishing empire renowned throughout the Chinese-speaking world. Later, Ping Xintao successively ventured into film, television, and the music industry, establishing companies such as the Firebird Film Company, Superstar Film Company, Pleasant Communication Company, Lovable Communication Company, and Lovable Record Company. In the late 1970s, Ping Xintao, along with Qiong Yao and others, jointly invested to establish the Superstar Film Company, specializing in adapting Qiong Yao's novels into films.

6

![Image 5: Ping Xintao was photographed in Florence in 1976.](https://gbaike-image.cdn.bcebos.com/e850352ac65c10387efbd1ddb8119313b07e8923/e850352ac65c10387efbd1ddb8119313b07e8923_url?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto/resize,m_lfit,h_1024,limit_1)

Ping Xintao was photographed in Florence in 1976.

Later Years

In 1998, Ping Xintao served as the producer of the television series My Fair Princess. In 1999, he served as the producer of the television series My Fair Princess II. In 2002, at the age of 75, Ping Xintao's health began to deteriorate. He served as the producer for the television series My Fair Princess III: Heaven and Earth, which aired in 2003. In 2014, on the occasion of celebrating the 60th anniversary of Crown magazine, a special issue of over 600 pages was produced. Ping Xintao, then nearly 90 years old, personally called writers to solicit contributions. In 2015, due to embolisms in the blood vessels of his brain, Ping Xintao's cognitive abilities began to decline rapidly; he could no longer understand many written texts and films, and his memory deteriorated sharply. In 2016, Ping Xintao was hospitalized for treatment of Vascular Dementia.

2

Death

Ping Xintao died on May 23, 2019, at the age of 92.

1

Personal Life

Marriage

Ping Xintao's first wife was Lin Wanzhen, with whom he had three children: a son named Ping Yun and two daughters named Ping Ying and Ping Heng. Lin Wanzhen was a painter from a wealthy family. When Ping Xintao co-founded the magazine Crown, she not only provided him with funds but also helped him recruit staff.

7

![Image 6: Ping Xintao, Lin Wanzhen, and their three children](https://gbaike-image.cdn.bcebos.com/b3fb43166d224f4a20a4f85c6bae87529822720e7b70/b3fb43166d224f4a20a4f85c6bae87529822720e7b70_url?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto/resize,m_lfit,h_1024,limit_1)

Ping Xintao, Lin Wanzhen, and their three children

Ping Xintao and Qiong Yao first met through manuscript submissions. In 1963, Qiong Yao gained popularity with her novel *Outside the Window* and met Ping Xintao. With Ping Xintao's full support, Qiong Yao quickly entered the first golden period of her career. In 1964, Qiong Yao divorced her husband, and later, Ping Xintao also divorced his wife. In 1979, Ping Xintao and Qiong Yao married. Qiong Yao turned down high-paying external writing offers and gave all her novel copyrights to Ping Xintao's Crown Publishing, making her husband her agent and publisher. In the 1990s, he and his wife Qiong Yao entered the film and television industry, specializing in adapting Qiong Yao's novels into movies and TV dramas. The combination of "Qiong Yao + Ping Xintao" extended from novels to film and television, known as the "Qiong Yao Economy."

5

![Image 7: Ping Xintao and Qiong Yao](https://gbaike-image.cdn.bcebos.com/3b292df5e0fe9925d9c2764f3ea85edf8cb171e6/3b292df5e0fe9925d9c2764f3ea85edf8cb171e6_url?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto/resize,m_lfit,h_1024,limit_1)

Ping Xintao and Qiong Yao

Personal Hobbies

Ping Xintao liked ducks and associated them with the publishing industry and the publishing philosophy of Crown. A special issue of the Crown magazine published a Duck Declaration, which stated: a duck is not a noble peacock or a rare phoenix; it is ordinary and down-to-earth, representing Crown Publishing's approachable and public-oriented style. A duck floats gracefully on the water's surface while its webbed feet paddle vigorously underneath. This image of a duck paddling aligns perfectly with the operational principles of the publishing industry. Ping Xintao always believed that the publishing industry is one that appears elegant on the surface while everyone exerts effort underneath. The competition among publishing houses is a peaceful one, far from being bloody.

14

Lucky Number

Ping Xintao's lucky number was "2". His birthday was on the 22nd. When he moved from Shanghai to Taipei in 1949, the number of his dormitory room was also 22. When founding the Crown magazine (February 1954), he wanted to break the convention of magazines being published at the beginning of the month and set the publication date of Crown magazine for the 22nd of each month.

14

Major Works

Translations

Ping Xintao's translations include Shane, Cousin Li Qiu, The Corpse Collision Record, among others.

13

| References 12 |

Notable Events

Anger over Plagiarism

At the beginning of the new year in 2005, Ping Xintao and Qiong Yao issued a joint statement expressing shock and indignation at a publisher on the Chinese mainland planning to publish a new book titled "Qiong Yao and Ping Xintao's Arduous Love". They stated that, apart from some material plagiarized from Qiong Yao's "My Story", the vast majority of the book consisted of the author's absurd speculations and fabricated text. The couple protested, asking: Where did their so-called "arduous love" come from? Therefore, in their statement, the couple declared that the book not only seriously violated copyright and portrait rights but also deceived a wide readership by distorting facts. Besides stating they would study taking necessary legal action, they also hoped the public and their caring readers would understand the truth. To learn about the sincere confessions between Qiong Yao and "Mr. Qiong Yao" and to know the details of their emotional journey from meeting, understanding, to falling in love, one should read the newly published "Against the Stream" on the mainland.

9

Regarding the Estate

On October 11, 2010, Ping Xintao personally went to Crown Publishing House to inform his three children about his will. It included instructions such as no emergency resuscitation or intubation if critically ill, and no obituary or funeral service after death. He allocated his estate: the Crown publishing portion was given to the Ping family children, while Keyuan and the film and television industry were left to his spouse, Qiong Yao.

8

Ping Xintao's son, Ping Yun, said: Keyuan (Qiong Yao's villa in Taipei, worth approximately 560 million RMB) was a gift from their father to Aunt Qiong Yao, and the film and television income from Crown also belonged to her; their father never took a single cent. Additionally, Ping Xintao's collections were distributed between Keyuan and the Crown Publishing House. As for the remaining real estate, some were pre-marital assets, and for post-marital assets, the spouse had a statutory reserved portion; these matters would be handled by lawyers according to the law. Besides property, Ping Yun mentioned that after his father's passing, there were trivial matters like deregistration and insurance to handle. He felt there should be no dispute with Qiong Yao, nor did he wish for any, hoping their father could rest in peace.

8

Family Dispute

Ping Xintao was hospitalized in 2016 due to Vascular Dementia. In 2017, Qiong Yao expressed her feelings on Facebook, stating that Ping Xintao's life had come to an end, but his children were unwilling to accept this fact. Knowing her husband could not recover and unable to bear the thought of him having a nasogastric tube inserted, Qiong Yao fell out with her stepchildren over this issue. Ping Xintao's son, Ping Yun, issued a statement via Facebook, clarifying that no doctor had ever declared Ping Xintao critically ill or in a deep coma; he was merely suffering from dementia, and they believed Qiong Yao simply could not accept their father's condition. Qiong Yao later responded to her stepchildren online in the form of an open letter. She began by "apologizing" to Ping Ying, Ping Heng, and Ping Yun, and even said she should not have met her husband Ping Xintao, leading to the division between the two families to this extent. She accused her stepchildren of fabricating facts, leaving her wanting to cry but having no tears. She stated she had never said the words, "Ping Xintao is already a body without a soul; from now on, please take care of him yourselves," claiming it was fabricated by her stepchildren. At the end of the open letter, Qiong Yao said she would temporarily not visit her husband to avoid emotional breakdown and informed the children about her husband's daily necessities and precautions. Later, in her newly published book "Before the Snow Falls", Qiong Yao poured out her grievances. She also retrieved the copyrights for 65 of her works from Crown and handed them over to the Cite Publishing Group for re-publication as "The Complete Works of Qiong Yao". Ping Xintao's ex-wife, Lin Wanzhen, published an autobiography, directly accusing Qiong Yao of destroying her family back then.

10

Evaluation

Ping Xintao valued and cherished talent, appreciating Qiong Yao. He successively published Qiong Yao's works such as Misty Rain, Outside the Window, and My Fair Princess. He also boldly adapted Qiong Yao's works into television series, with productions like My Fair Princess and Dreams Link becoming immensely popular across the country. The lead actors, Ruby Lin, Zhao Wei, Su Youpeng, and others, remain active on screen to this day. (Daily Economic News)
